description.narrative: The San Alonso Rodríguez Foundation (FSAR) promotes in the department of Colón, Honduras, an alternative development model focused on social, gender and environmental justice, with an emphasis on the defense of human rights and the valorization of local knowledge. Their project will directly benefit 390 people – mainly women and youth – and indirectly more than 19,000 inhabitants of the Aguán region. The project seeks to improve the conditions and quality of life of peasant, indigenous, and Garifuna families by promoting a cooperative-productive model with climate justice, gender equity, and community capacity building. Its actions are aimed at guaranteeing rights to habitat, food and a healthy environment; strengthening the political and productive leadership of women and youth; and to strengthen the organization, management and marketing of groups linked to housing, production and transformation. It is expected that the families involved will improve their productive and environmental practices, that the communities will strengthen their capacity for advocacy and that several cooperative groups will consolidate sustainable economic initiatives.
